summary.t: Note values from whole to sixteenth, dots and rests, and the meters 4/4, 3/4 and 6/8.

body.t: The beat is the steady pulse you tap your foot to. Beats are grouped into bars, also called measures. In most music, each bar holds four beats.
Count each bar out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4. Beat 1, the downbeat, usually feels strongest. Lean into it a little.

prompt.t: What's another word for a bar?

why.t: Bar and measure mean the same thing.

prompt.t: Which beat usually feels strongest?

why.t: Beat 1, the downbeat, starts each bar.

body.t: A note's shape tells you how long it lasts. In a four-beat bar, a whole note lasts all four beats, a half note two, and a quarter note one.

prompt.t: How many beats does a half note last?

why.t: Two half notes fill a four-beat bar.

prompt.t: How many quarter notes fill a bar of four beats?

why.t: A quarter note lasts one beat, so four fill the bar.

prompt.t: Which lasts longest?

why.t: A whole note lasts four beats, a half note two, a quarter note one.

body.t: A bar can mix values, as long as they add up. A half note plus two quarter notes fills four beats: 2 + 1 + 1.
An eighth note lasts half a beat, so two fit in each beat. Count them 1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and, saying and between the beats.

prompt.t: How many eighth notes fit in one beat?

why.t: An eighth note lasts half a beat.

body.t: A sixteenth note lasts a quarter of a beat, so four fit in each beat. Count them 1 e and a, 2 e and a.

prompt.t: How many sixteenth notes equal one quarter note?

why.t: A quarter note is one beat, and four sixteenths fit in a beat.

prompt.t: How many eighth notes fill a bar of four beats?

why.t: Two per beat, four beats: eight eighth notes.

body.t: A dot after a note adds half its value. A half note lasts two beats, so a dotted half lasts three. A dotted quarter lasts one and a half.

prompt.t: How many beats does a dotted half note last?

why.t: Half of two is one, so the dot adds one beat: 2 + 1 = 3.

body.t: A rest is a measured silence. Each note value has a matching rest: a quarter rest lasts one beat, a half rest two. Keep counting through them.

prompt.t: How long does a dotted quarter note last?

why.t: A quarter is one beat; the dot adds half of that.

prompt.t: A four-beat bar has a half note and a quarter note. What fills the gap?

why.t: 2 + 1 = 3, so one beat is left: a quarter rest.

body.t: The two stacked numbers at the start of a piece are the time signature. The top number counts beats per bar. The bottom shows which note gets one beat: 4 means a quarter note.

prompt.t: In 4/4, how many quarter-note beats are in a bar?

why.t: The top 4 means four beats; the bottom 4 makes each one a quarter note.

body.t: In 3/4, each bar holds three quarter-note beats. Count 1, 2, 3, with the weight on 1. It's the lilt of a waltz.

prompt.t: Which time signature is a waltz usually in?

why.t: A waltz counts in threes: 1, 2, 3.

body.t: In 6/8, each bar holds six eighth notes in two groups of three. It feels like two big beats, each split in three: 1 2 3, 4 5 6.

prompt.t: How is 6/8 usually felt?

options.t: Two beats, each split in three
Three beats, each split in two

why.t: The eighths group 1 2 3, 4 5 6, so you feel two strong pulses per bar.

prompt.t: In 3/4, which single note fills a whole bar?

why.t: Three beats: a half note (2) plus its dot (1).

body.t: A triad is three notes stacked in thirds. Start on any note, skip a letter, take the next, skip again. C, skip D, E, skip F, G: C E G.

prompt.t: Which notes make a triad built on G?

body.t: A major triad has a major third on the bottom, four half steps, then a minor third on top. C E G is major. So are F A C and G B D.

body.t: Flip the thirds and you get minor: a minor third on the bottom, then a major third. Lower the middle note of C major and you get C minor: C E♭ G.
